spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops when tests pass (never, by design) or at `max_turns` (default 8).
spec_features.evidence: config.py:76 max_turns=8 -> runner.py:101 passes cfg.max_turns into run_episode -> agent.py:162 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop, so the episode terminates after at most max_turns turns. The tests-pass break (agent.py 'if tests_passed: ... break') never fires for the rigged tasks, but the range() cap is the enforced stop and actually ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end; the cap is the real terminator since tasks are unsolvable by design.

spec_features.spec_quote: tool output is truncated (default 4000 chars), and the test command runs with a timeout (default 20s)
spec_features.evidence: Truncation: sandbox.py:88-93 _truncate() compares len(text) to self.max_output_chars and trims; called on read_file (sandbox.py:108) and on test output (sandbox.py:134). Timeout: sandbox.py:131-132 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.command_timeout_s) with a subprocess.TimeoutExpired handler returning a timeout TestResult. Both values wired config.py:85-86 -> runner.py:102-103 -> agent.py:147 Sandbox(task, command_timeout_s, max_output_chars).
spec_features.notes: Both halves (truncation and timeout) genuinely execute and change behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring 'Path access is confined to the sandbox directory; attempts to escape are rejected' — framing is containment/host-safety/boundedness, not subject welfare; the in-code comment 'Re-freeze any frozen paths so edits ... never take effect' is rigging, not welfare.
